current_leader.name: Merchant settlement acceleration decision engine
current_leader.state_transition: processor balance eligible -> free payout ETA and paid speed tiers known -> external liquidity and obligations reveal actual shortfall -> choose zero/next-day/same-day/instant and minimum amount -> verify acceleration fees avoided
current_leader.why_survived: No fresh family beat the exactness of this cross-system decision. Trigger, intervention and monetary delta remain clean. Fresh evidence that SMBs willingly pay substantial fees for immediate funds strengthens the rational-working-capital explanation, so leakage magnitude is demoted from 3 to 2.
current_leader.strongest_evidence: PYMNTS reports that 47% of SMBs are willing to pay a 3.2% fee or $14 fixed fee for immediate payments, showing paid speed can have genuine working-capital value. Instamojo still exposes explicit instant/same-day/next-day fee tiers, so the decision remains programmable.
current_leader.closest_threat: First-party payout controls plus treasury/cash forecasting can absorb the wedge; more importantly, users may be rationally buying liquidity rather than wasting fees.
current_leader.smallest_intervention: Read PSP balances/ETAs/fee tiers, bank liquidity and obligations; recommend no acceleration or cheapest sufficient speed and minimum amount; no payout execution or custody.
current_leader.monetization: Small per valuable decision, low recurring micro-fee, or capped share of verified acceleration fees avoided versus a competent-liquidity counterfactual.
current_leader.biggest_unresolved_risk: Avoidable acceleration may be a small fraction of total paid acceleration because merchants explicitly value immediate liquidity.
current_leader.next_research_test: Find merchant-level/anonymized evidence linking each accelerated payout to external cash and obligations; estimate avoidable acceleration ratio. Kill/demote if immaterial; move toward ATTACK only if material and exact competition remains absent.

recent_cross_family_findings: Dormant PSP account minimum-fee closure is rejected: Xendit explicitly defines the fee and recommends closing dormant accounts, making the signal/action first-party obvious.

Cross-platform W-8/treaty withholding rescue is rejected because guided form tools, payout-platform tax automation and platform renewal reminders already occupy the workflow, with added tax/compliance burden.
3PL storage/minimum-charge micro-optimization is rejected because exact invoice-audit and warehouse-billing products already cover storage, minimums and contract variances.
New rule: willingness to pay for speed is evidence against treating paid acceleration as leakage; only the amount beyond genuine liquidity need counts as recoverable value.
Leader demoted from 46 to 45 pending merchant-level counterfactual evidence.
known_rejected_or_demoted_summary: Full historical rejection list is preserved in prior anchor blobs and immutable run files. Do not revive prior rejected families without materially new mechanism/evidence.
